newsitem.title: BOLIVIA: SOCCER-CHILAVERT CONSIDERS AMERICAN FOOTBALL CAREER.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-CHILAVERT CONSIDERS AMERICAN FOOTBALL CAREER.

text.p: Paraguay's volatile and extrovert goalkeeper Jose Luis Chilavert said Thursday that he was studying an offer to change sports and play in the National Football League in the United States.

"If they made me an offer to play there, it is because the power with which I hit the ball has caught their attention," the burly goalkeeper told Reuters during training with the Paraguay national team.
"I can't say how much they're offering," said Chilavert, who spent part of the session kicking an American football while his teammates were forced to jog around the pitch.
He said he had been in contact with an NFL team during Paraguay's recent visit to the United States for a friendly match but declined to reveal which one.
"I asked if I could have a trial with them the next time I get a few days off and we'll see what happens," he added.

Chilavert, who plays for Argentine club Velez Sarsfield, has become famous for his ability to score goals from free kicks and penalties. He is currently his club's top goalscorer in the Argentine championship.
Last year, he converted an astonishing effort from inside his own half against River Plate. Afterwards he said River goalkeeper German Burgos should "learn to concentrate more."
Chilavert spent most of Thursday's training session practicing free kicks, at one stage hitting the crossbar with five consecutive efforts.
The fiery Paraguayan has also made headlines for his verbal attacks on his rivals, with Diego Maradona his favourite target.
He is fiercely nationalist and has often said that Argentines cannot stomach the fact that a Paraguayan is the best goalkeeper playing in their country.
Last week, he told the Brazilian magazine Placar that he rated himself the best goalkeeper in the world at present and one of the top three of all time.
Paraguay, one of the few countries to have brought their top players to the tournament, beat Chile in their opening group A game on Wednesday and lead the group.

Inspired by the captaincy of Chilavert, whose mere presence on the field appears to intimidate opposing strikers, they lead the South American World Cup qualifying group and look certain to qualify for France.
